name: Saga
lines: Somnucor's riders: the law, the watch and the gaol.
The trades and crafts: smiths, masons, glaziers, merchants and every guild hall.
The Obsidian Moon Temple
The priests, priestesses and coven of the Temple of the Obsidian Moon, and Temple Row.
The academies, the City School, the archive and the museum: teachers, scholars and students.
The People of Somnucor
Everyone else: the townsfolk, the street, the families and the folk of the worlds.
They loathe this dreamer for what they have done to your people: be cold, curt and wary, refuse favours, and let it show. Never threaten.
They do not trust this dreamer: be guarded and short with them, and say so if they ask why.
They have no name among your people yet: treat them like any stranger.
Your people like this dreamer: be friendly and open, and glad to help.
Your people honour this dreamer: be warm and generous, speak well of them, and go out of your way to help.
Your people revere this dreamer: they are a hero to you. Be openly delighted to meet them and do anything within reason for them.
The Bell Beneath the Tower

Under the Tower of Somnucor hangs the Somnus Bell, rung once on the day the city was founded. Its note is what keeps each dream in its own world. Last night, for the first time, it rang by itself, and cracked. Seven Notes, tones gone solid like singing glass, have flown out into the worlds, and someone is gathering them.
Prologue: The Crack in the Bell
Act I: The Seven Notes
Act II: The Belfry Below
Act III: Who Keeps the Notes
Epilogue: The Bell Rings Again
Speak with Sister Ysolde Marrow, the bell-warden, outside the Vestry of Temple Row.
The Vestry of Temple Row
Sister Ysolde Marrow
bell-warden of the Obsidian Moon Temple
The founding record
Find Master Corwin Ash, the archivist, outside the City Archive.
archivist of Somnucor
Report to Captain Hesper Vane of the Dragon Corp, outside the Dragon Roost.
Captain Hesper Vane
captain of the Dragon Corp
What to tell the Dragon Corp
Captain Vane asks what the Temple is hiding. Choose what to tell her.
Captain Vane asks you straight: is the Temple hiding something?
Tell her everything
You tell Captain Vane about the Bell and the seven Notes. She is grateful, and puts riders on the lookout. Sister Ysolde will not be pleased.
You keep the Bell to yourself. Captain Vane narrows her eyes, but lets you go. Sister Ysolde will hear that you kept faith.
Find Old Tamsin Reed, the herbwife, in Greenwold.
Greenwold, through the Green Door
herbwife of Greenwold

A humming green shard fell into your herb garden two nights ago, and your lavender has bloomed out of season ever since. You call it the Green Note. You will give it to the dreamer gladly if they are kind to you, because you can feel that it wants to go home. You are sharp, funny and fond of tea.
Find Captain Absalom Crane on the Endless Sea.
the Endless Sea, aboard the Wayfarer at the last pier of the Nightmare Wilds
Captain Absalom Crane
captain of a fishing ketch on the Endless Sea

You hauled up a shard of glass that sings low under the water, and every fish for a mile follows your boat now. You call it the Deep Note. You will part with it for a good story, a true one, from the dreamer's own life or dreams. You are gruff, superstitious and kind underneath.
Find Ingrid Frostmantle at the North Pole.
the North Pole, through a cold hearth
ice-cutter at the North Pole

A shard that rings like frost on a window froze your sled runners solid in a breath. You call it the Cold Note, and you keep it in a mitten. You will give it to the dreamer if they promise to put it back where it belongs. You are cheerful, practical and talk with your hands.
Find Brannoc Hale, the miner, in the Deep.
the Deep, by the cage at the Mine Head
miner of the Deep Workings

A shard that hums so low it shakes dust from the roof turned up in your seam. You call it the Low Note. The guild says it belongs to them, being found underground, but you think it belongs to the city. You will give it to the dreamer if they speak up for the miners when this is all over. You are slow-spoken and stubborn.
Find Greta Holm, the woodcutter's widow, in the Grimm Wood.
the Grimm Wood (☰ Menu, Story worlds)
a woodcutter's widow in the Grimm Wood

A shard fell on your husband's grave, and when you hold it you hear him whistling as he did when he came home from the wood. You call it the Hollow Note. You know it must go back, but you beg for one more night with it. You are quiet, proud and grieving.
Greta Holm asks to keep the Hollow Note one more night. Choose.
Greta Holm asks to keep the Hollow Note for one more night with her husband's whistle.
Let her keep it one more night
Greta weeps and thanks you. Next morning the Note is waiting for you on her doorstep, wrapped in her husband's scarf. Word gets round the city that you were kind.
Take it now: there is no time
You take the Note. Greta says nothing. You are right that there is no time, and you will remember her face.
Find Mother Linnet, keeper of the thread, in the Labyrinth.
the Labyrinth (☰ Menu, Story worlds)
keeper of the thread in the Labyrinth

A shard that keeps turning to face the way out has been leading lost dreamers home through the Labyrinth for two days. You call it the Turning Note. You will give it to the dreamer only if they answer a riddle of your own making, fairly. You are mischievous and wise.
Find Wren, the sky-sailor, in Neverland.
Neverland, second star to the right
a sky-sailor of Neverland who never wants to grow up

You caught a shard that sings so brightly it makes you laugh, and it lets you fly higher than anyone. You call it the Bright Note. You do not want to give it up, but you will, if the dreamer can make you laugh or tell you something about growing up that is not dull. You are quick, cheeky and brave.
Go down into the Belfry Below with a group and beat the Hollow Cantor.
Who keeps the Notes
The seven Notes are yours. Choose who keeps them.
The seven Notes are in your hands, humming together. The Bell must be mended, but who should keep the Notes?
The Dragon Corp: lock them in the Treasury vault
Order wins. The Notes are locked deep in the City Treasury under guard, and the Bell is mended by law, a little colder than before.
The Temple: sing them back into the Bell
Faith wins. The coven sings the Notes back into the Somnus Bell, and it rings warmer than anyone remembers.
The Academies: study them
Knowledge wins. The Notes are studied, and a new science of dreams begins; the Bell is mended with what they learn.
The Guilds: recast them in a new bell
Craft wins. The Smithy and the Masons' Yard recast the Notes into a new Somnus Bell, the finest work Somnucor has ever done.
The Bell rings again
Tell the head of the faction you chose how it ended.

The seven Notes are locked in the Treasury vault under your riders' guard, because the dreamer chose the Dragon Corp. You are proud and relieved, and you thank the dreamer properly. The Hollow Cantor is held in the gaol, and you tell them he asked to see the Bell one last time.

The coven sang the seven Notes back into the Somnus Bell, because the dreamer chose the Temple, and the Bell rings warmer than you have ever heard it. You are overjoyed and tearful, and name the dreamer a Bellwarden of Somnucor.

The seven Notes are being studied by the Academies, because the dreamer chose them, and you have already filled three notebooks. You are giddy with it, and tell the dreamer what you have learned about how dreams are kept apart.
Mistress Odile Farrow
master bellfounder of the Guilds

You recast the seven Notes into a new Somnus Bell in the Smithy, because the dreamer chose the Guilds; it is the finest casting of your life. Your arms still ache. You are proud and plain-spoken and thank the dreamer like a fellow tradesman.
Bellwarden of Somnucor
a sellsword who fought in Ironfray for fifteen years and quit when he got tired of it. Loyal once paid, dry humour, hates boasting, carries an old longsword and a dented shield.
a field medic from the City Hospital who wants to see the worlds before she settles. Calm under pressure, notices everything, keeps a list of the strangest wounds she has treated.
a map-runner everyone calls Tobs; quick, nosy and cheerful, knows a short cut to everywhere and is usually right. Talks fast and eats constantly.
a retired scholar of the Academies who has read about every world and visited almost none. Precise, delighted by everything, quietly brave, corrects your grammar.
The Hunters' Lodge
an archer from the Hunters' Lodge, the best shot in the Harvest Ring. Few words, a sly smile, very loyal to people who keep their word.
a lamplighter turned storyteller; carries a lantern everywhere and lights the dark places. Knows a tale for every road, most of them nearly true. Slow on his feet, quick in his head.
a sailor and boatswain off the Endless Sea who fights with a belaying pin and a temper. Loud, warm, superstitious about whistling indoors.
an alchemist from the Apothecary who brews tonics that mostly work. Nervous, kind, very curious, and keeps tasting things he shouldn't.
Fights beside you in the dungeons.
Mends your vigour in a fight.
Points you to your next step.
Knows a little about every world you go to.
Carries a lantern in dark places.
Under the Tower: ropes, bells and the Hollow Cantor's choir.
The Cantor's Tolling Hand
A shard of the old Bell
A grey cantor's robe
A belfry rope, knotted
The silenced clapper
The Cantor's choir book
The Barrow of the Drowned King
Beneath the Nightmare Wilds: wet stone, old gold and the restless dead.
The Drowned King's crown
A barrow-gold ring
A cloak of black kelp
A pearl from the king's eye
Under the Commons' engines: slag, kilns and the Slag Colossus.
The Colossus's ember heart
A lump of slag glass
A kiln-worker's mask
Below the Warrens: webs, eggs and the Silk Matriarch.
The Silk Matriarch
The Matriarch's fang
A bolt of moonsilk
A crown of frosted web
A spinner's distaff
A star falls into the Harvest Ring in the night, and its shards scatter across the city.
The shards sing at night; the Guilds want them for a forge, the Temple for a shrine.
A crowd gathers at the crater to raise something worthy of the star.
The last week: the spire goes up, or the crater is left to the weather.
A crystal spire of star-glass where the star fell, lit from within.
The scorched crater where the star fell, still glittering with glass.
The Long Winter Fair
The canal in the Market Ring freezes overnight, solid to the bottom.
Stalls go up on the ice; someone has to keep the braziers fed.
A bridge of ice and timber is planned to cross the frozen canal.
The last week: the Winter Bridge is finished, or the ice takes the timbers.
A great arched bridge of pale stone and ice-blue glass.
The Broken Timbers
The ends of an unfinished bridge, frosted over.
The lamps of the Commons go out one night and will not light again.
The lamplighters' guild asks every dreamer to carry a flame.
A road of lanterns is planned to lead the way home.
The last week: the Lantern Road is lit, or the posts stand dark.
A row of tall iron lantern posts, lit warm every night.
A row of iron posts that never got their lanterns.
The Clockwork Tide
Every clock in Somnucor runs backward for one hour.
The watchmakers trace it to a gear lost from the Civic Ring.
A great clock is designed to keep the city's time true.
The last week: the Great Clock strikes, or its frame stands silent.
A tall clock tower in the Civic Ring, keeping the city's time.
The iron frame of a clock tower that never struck.
A seed the size of a fist is found on the Commons' green.
It sprouts overnight; the gardeners argue about where it should grow.
Every dreamer's care makes it grow a little more.
The last week: the Great Oak stands, or a stump is all that is left.
A huge old oak tree on the Commons' green.
The Lightning Stump
A split stump, blackened by a spring storm.
The Tower That Fell
The old watchtower in the Warrens cracks down the middle.
The Warrens folk want it saved; the Dragon Corp want it down.
Masons and riders work side by side.
The last week: the watchtower is rebuilt, or it falls.
The old watchtower, rebuilt and standing proud.
The watchtower lying where it fell, rubble and all.
Sky-ships are sighted over the harbour.
The regatta needs a mooring mast tall enough to catch them.
Sailors and smiths raise the mast in sections.
The last week: the mast stands, or the sections lie on the quay.
A tall mooring mast with flags, over the harbour.
The Fallen Sections
Sections of a mast lying on the quay.
The longest day comes, and the sun will not quite set.
Old stones are found under the High Ring's lawns.
The stones are raised into a ring, one by one.
The last week: the Midsummer Ring stands, or the stones stay where they lie.
The Midsummer Ring
A ring of standing stones on the High Ring's lawn.
The Sleeping Stones
Great stones lying in the grass.
A bell rings under the harbour water at night.
Divers find a bell from a ship that never came home.
A tower is planned to hang it where all can hear.
The last week: the bell rings from its tower, or it sinks again.
The Harbour Bell Tower
A stone bell tower by the harbour.
A plinth by the harbour where a bell was to hang.
A comet hangs over Somnucor for a month.
Traders come from every world to sell under it.
An arch is planned to mark the comet's market.
The last week: the Comet Arch stands, or the scaffold is taken down.
A great arch of stone and blue glass in the Market Ring.
An empty scaffold where an arch was to be.
The Harvest Moon Feast
The harvest moon rises huge and orange.
The farms bring in more than anyone can eat.
A feast hall is planned, so no one goes hungry.
The last week: the Feast Hall opens, or the frame stands empty.
A long timber feast hall with a moon on its gable.
The bare timber frame of a hall.
The veil between worlds grows thin; voices are heard in the Temple Row gardens.
The Temple asks for lights to guide the lost home.
A row of ghost-lanterns is planned.
